nutrients.mechanism: Marine omega-3 intake is associated with reduced anginal frequency and improved lipid/inflammatory profile as part of a Mediterranean-pattern diet for secondary CVD prevention.
nutrients.dosage: 1-2 g/day combined EPA/DHA from oily fish or algal oil, alongside a Mediterranean dietary pattern
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High doses (>3 g/day) can potentiate antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs -- common in this population; discuss with cardiologist.
nutrients.source: Estruch R et al., Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease with a Mediterranean Diet Supplemented with Extra-Virgin Olive Oil or Nuts (PREDIMED), N Engl J Med 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Soluble fibre lowers LDL cholesterol, a modifiable driver of atherosclerotic angina.
nutrients.dosage: 10 g/day soluble fibre (oats, psyllium, legumes)
nutrients.foodSources: Psyllium Husk / Isabgol (dried) (71g, 710.0% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (ground) (11g, 110.0% RDA); Chia Seeds (dried) (10g, 100.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Introduce gradually with fluids to avoid bloating.
nutrients.source: Brum J et al., meta-analysis of psyllium fibre as adjuvant antilipid therapy, Am J Cardiol 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Restricting dietary sodium reduces fluid retention and lowers the workload on a failing heart; benefit on hard outcomes is more modest than once assumed (SODIUM-HF, 2022).
nutrients.dosage: <2,000-3,000 mg/day (specialist-individualised; avoid <1,500 mg/day, which can worsen outcomes in some patients)
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do not over-restrict -- aggressive sodium/fluid restriction can trigger hyponatraemia and neurohormonal activation. Individualise with a cardiologist/dietitian.
nutrients.source: ESC Heart Failure Guidelines 2021 (dietary sodium restriction, moderate evidence) + SODIUM-HF trial (Ezekowitz 2022)

nutrients.mechanism: Chronic loop-diuretic use (furosemide etc., mainstay of HF therapy) depletes thiamine; correcting a deficiency can improve cardiac function in affected patients.
nutrients.dosage: Screen if on long-term high-dose loop diuretics; replace per deficiency (100-300 mg/day short course if confirmed low)
nutrients.foodSources: Nutritional Yeast (14.3mg, 1243.5% RDA); Flour, all-purpose, enriched (1.9mg, 167.0% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (1.6mg, 142.6% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Not a substitute for guideline-directed medical therapy; supplement only if deficiency is confirmed or strongly suspected.
nutrients.source: NIH ODS Thiamin Fact Sheet -- diuretic-associated depletion in heart failure

nutrients.mechanism: Increased salt (and fluid) intake expands blood volume, the first-line non-drug measure to reduce vasovagal syncope frequency.
nutrients.dosage: Increase dietary salt as advised by a clinician (often to ~2,300-3,000 mg/day) plus 2-2.5 L fluids/day, unless contraindicated (e.g. hypertension, renal or heart disease)
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Contraindicated or needs supervision in hypertension, heart failure, or kidney disease.
nutrients.source: ESC Guidelines on the diagnosis and management of syncope 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Liberalising salt and fluid intake expands plasma volume and is first-line non-pharmacological therapy for orthostatic hypotension.
nutrients.dosage: 6-10 g salt/day and 2-2.5 L fluid/day (specialist-guided), plus a 500 mL bolus of water before rising if needed
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Avoid in uncontrolled hypertension or heart failure; monitor supine BP.
nutrients.source: ESC/EFNS guidance on orthostatic hypotension management

nutrients.mechanism: Low vitamin D is associated with more frequent/severe asthma exacerbations in observational studies; trial evidence for supplementation reducing exacerbations is positive mainly in deficient patients and mixed overall (VDAART and related trials).
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency; not evidence-supported as routine high-dose therapy without testing
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Adjunct only -- inhaled therapy remains the primary evidence-based asthma treatment; this does not apply to the acute exacerbation itself, only longer-term deficiency correction.
nutrients.source: Jolliffe DA et al., individual participant data meta-analysis, Lancet Respir Med 2017

nutrients.mechanism: Unintentional weight loss and sarcopenia are common in COPD and worsen exacerbation outcomes; higher protein/energy intake supports respiratory muscle mass and recovery.
nutrients.dosage: 1.2-1.5 g protein/kg body weight/day if underweight or losing muscle mass
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Needs dietitian input if renal impairment coexists.
nutrients.source: GOLD Global Strategy for COPD -- nutritional support in underweight patients

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin D deficiency is common in COPD and correlates with exacerbation frequency in observational studies; RCT evidence for reducing exacerbations is mixed and positive mainly in deficient patients.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency (typically 800-2,000 IU/day); routine supplementation without testing is not established
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap -- benefit is not established in vitamin D-replete patients.
nutrients.source: Jolliffe DA et al., meta-analysis of individual participant data, Thorax 2019

nutrients.mechanism: Regular vitamin C does not prevent colds in the general population, but modestly shortens duration and severity once a cold has started.
nutrients.dosage: 1-2 g/day at symptom onset (regular prophylactic use only clearly helps in people under heavy physical stress, e.g. marathon runners, cold-weather troops)
nutrients.foodSources: Amla / Indian Gooseberry (raw) (600mg, 722.9% RDA); Guava / Amrood (raw) (228mg, 274.7% RDA); peppers, bell, red, raw, mini (220.5mg, 265.7% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High doses can cause GI upset; caution with history of oxalate kidney stones.
nutrients.source: Hemila & Chalker, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2013, CD000980.pub4

nutrients.mechanism: Zinc lozenges/syrup started within 24 hours of symptom onset can shorten cold duration; the older Singh & Das Cochrane review (2013) was withdrawn in 2015 for methodological errors -- the current, more cautious Cochrane review (2024) still finds a modest benefit.
nutrients.dosage: >75 mg/day elemental zinc in divided doses (lozenge form), started within 24h of symptoms, for no more than a few days
nutrients.foodSources: Oysters (cooked) (78.6mg, 786.0% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (10mg, 100.0% RDA); Hemp Seeds / Bhang (hulled) (9.9mg, 99.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Intranasal zinc products have caused permanent loss of smell -- avoid. Nausea is common at these doses.
nutrients.source: Nault D et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2024, CD014914.pub2

nutrients.mechanism: Cancer-related cachexia (muscle wasting) is common in lung cancer and worsens treatment tolerance and outcomes; higher protein/energy intake, ideally with dietitian support, is part of standard supportive oncology care.
nutrients.dosage: 1.2-2.0 g protein/kg/day as tolerated, individualised with an oncology dietitian
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Does not treat the cancer itself -- this is supportive care alongside oncology-directed treatment; individual tolerance varies greatly during chemo/radiotherapy.
nutrients.source: ESPEN Guideline on Clinical Nutrition in Cancer

nutrients.mechanism: Malnutrition both predisposes to and results from active TB; nutritional support improves treatment completion and survival, and WHO recommends nutritional assessment/support as standard of care.
nutrients.dosage: Adequate energy and 1.2-1.5 g protein/kg/day during treatment; address any Vitamin D/other deficiencies found
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Nutritional support does not replace anti-TB drug therapy.
nutrients.source: WHO Guideline: Nutritional care and support for patients with tuberculosis (2013)

nutrients.mechanism: Magnesium deficiency is common in migraineurs; supplementation reduces attack frequency, rated 'probably effective' (Level B) by the AAN/American Headache Society.
nutrients.dosage: 400-600 mg/day magnesium citrate/oxide as a preventive course
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (627mg, 171.8% RDA); Pumpkin Seeds / Kaddu Beej (dried) (592mg, 162.2% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (511mg, 140.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Can cause diarrhoea at higher doses; reduce dose if this occurs. Caution in renal impairment.
nutrients.source: AAN/AHS Evidence-based guideline update: NSAIDs and complementary treatments for episodic migraine prevention (2012)

nutrients.mechanism: High-dose riboflavin improves mitochondrial energy metabolism thought to be impaired in migraine, reducing attack frequency (Level B evidence).
nutrients.dosage: 400 mg/day for at least 3 months
nutrients.foodSources: Nutritional Yeast (9.7mg, 808.3% RDA); Beef Liver (cooked) (3.4mg, 283.3% RDA); Chicken Liver (cooked) (2.3mg, 191.7% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Harmless at this dose; may cause bright-yellow urine (benign).
nutrients.source: AAN/AHS guideline (2012) + Cochrane-level nutraceutical reviews

nutrients.mechanism: This is secondary-prevention nutrition (reducing recurrence risk), not acute-phase treatment -- sodium restriction and a potassium-rich, Mediterranean/DASH-style diet reduce blood pressure and recurrent stroke risk.
nutrients.dosage: <2,300 mg/day sodium once medically stable and swallow-safe; started well after the acute emergency phase
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Not relevant to acute management -- swallow assessment and emergency stroke protocols take priority; this applies to the recovery/secondary-prevention phase only.
nutrients.source: AHA/ASA 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack

nutrients.mechanism: As for stroke, a low-sodium, potassium-rich dietary pattern is evidence-based secondary prevention against a future stroke after TIA.
nutrients.dosage: <2,300 mg/day sodium as part of a DASH/Mediterranean-pattern diet
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Secondary-prevention framing only -- does not apply to acute TIA assessment, which needs urgent same-day medical review regardless.
nutrients.source: AHA/ASA 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack

nutrients.mechanism: A low-sodium diet is the most widely recommended dietary measure for Meniere's disease, thought to reduce endolymphatic fluid pressure, though the evidence base is thin.
nutrients.dosage: <1,500-2,000 mg/day, trialled for 2-3 months
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: AAO-HNS's own 2020 guideline is candid that supporting evidence is limited; do not over-restrict to the point of risking hyponatraemia.
nutrients.source: AAO-HNS Clinical Practice Guideline: Meniere's Disease (2020)

nutrients.mechanism: The ketogenic diet (very high fat, very low carbohydrate) has good trial evidence for reducing seizure frequency in drug-resistant epilepsy, historically strongest in children; evidence in adults is weaker.
nutrients.dosage: Medically supervised ketogenic or modified Atkins diet -- requires specialist dietitian/neurology oversight, not a self-directed change
nutrients.foodSources: Mustard Oil / Sarson Ka Tel (100g, 153.8% RDA); Ghee / Clarified Butter (99.8g, 153.5% RDA); Oil, coconut (99.4g, 152.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Must be medically supervised -- risks include growth impairment (children), kidney stones, dyslipidaemia; only for drug-resistant epilepsy, not first-line for a new/single seizure.
nutrients.source: Martin-McGill KJ et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2020, ketogenic diets for drug-resistant epilepsy

nutrients.mechanism: B12 deficiency is a well-established, reversible cause of peripheral neuropathy; correcting it is curative for the deficiency-driven component of neuropathy (though not for neuropathy from other causes, e.g. diabetes, which needs separate management).
nutrients.dosage: IM B12 injections for confirmed deficiency (loading then maintenance per local protocol), or high-dose oral if pernicious anaemia is excluded/absorption is intact
nutrients.foodSources: Clams (cooked) (98.9mcg, 4120.8% RDA); Beef Liver (cooked) (83.1mcg, 3462.5% RDA); Anchovies, canned in olive oil, with salt, drained (22.8mcg, 950.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Only effective for the B12-deficiency component -- neuropathy from diabetes, chemotherapy or other causes needs its own management.
nutrients.source: NIH ODS Vitamin B12 Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

nutrients.mechanism: Low vitamin D is a well-replicated MS risk factor and is associated with relapse rate in observational studies; RCT evidence for supplementation reducing relapses is promising but not yet conclusive enough to be sole therapy.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency; many neurologists target higher-normal levels in MS patients, but there is no single agreed high-dose regimen -- follow the treating neurologist's protocol
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Not a substitute for disease-modifying MS drugs -- adjunct only.
nutrients.source: Sintzel MB et al., Vitamin D and Multiple Sclerosis: A Comprehensive Review, Neurology and Therapy 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Zinc supplementation shortens diarrhoea duration and reduces persistence beyond day 7 in children over 6 months old, especially where zinc deficiency is common; benefit is negligible under 6 months.
nutrients.dosage: WHO/UNICEF: 20 mg/day (10 mg under 6 months) for 10-14 days
nutrients.foodSources: Oysters (cooked) (78.6mg, 786.0% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (10mg, 100.0% RDA); Hemp Seeds / Bhang (hulled) (9.9mg, 99.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: No proven benefit in well-nourished adults; the strongest evidence is in children in low-/middle-income settings.
nutrients.source: Lazzerini M, Wanzira H. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2016, CD005436.pub5

nutrients.mechanism: Oral rehydration solution (sodium + potassium + glucose in a specific ratio) is the single most evidence-based intervention in acute gastroenteritis, correcting dehydration and electrolyte loss.
nutrients.dosage: WHO-formula ORS, replacing ongoing losses, ad-lib
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do not use plain water or sugary drinks alone for rehydration in significant dehydration -- electrolyte ratio matters.
nutrients.source: WHO/UNICEF Joint Statement: Clinical Management of Acute Diarrhoea

nutrients.mechanism: Soluble fibre (psyllium/ispaghula) improves global IBS symptoms, particularly constipation-predominant IBS; insoluble/wheat bran fibre can worsen bloating and is not recommended.
nutrients.dosage: Psyllium husk 10-20 g/day, titrated slowly
nutrients.foodSources: Psyllium Husk / Isabgol (dried) (71g, 710.0% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (ground) (11g, 110.0% RDA); Chia Seeds (dried) (10g, 100.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Insoluble fibre (wheat bran) often worsens IBS symptoms -- specifically favour soluble sources.
nutrients.source: Moayyedi P et al., The effect of fiber supplementation on irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis, Am J Gastroenterol 2014

nutrients.mechanism: A low-FODMAP diet (restricting fermentable oligo-, di-, monosaccharides and polyols -- a subset of dietary carbohydrate) reduces symptoms in the majority of IBS patients in RCTs.
nutrients.dosage: Structured low-FODMAP elimination (2-6 weeks) then supervised reintroduction, ideally dietitian-led
nutrients.foodSources: Sugars, granulated (99.6g, 76.6% RDA); Flour, cassava (87.3g, 67.2% RDA); Fonio, grain, dry, raw (81.3g, 62.5% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Not intended as a long-term restrictive diet -- reintroduction phase is essential to avoid unnecessary restriction and nutrient gaps.
nutrients.source: Monash University FODMAP research summary

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin D deficiency is very common in IBD and observational data link low levels with higher disease activity; correcting deficiency is standard of care though it is not a primary disease-modifying therapy.
nutrients.dosage: Correct confirmed deficiency (typically 800-2,000 IU/day, higher if malabsorptive)
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Malabsorption in active small-bowel Crohn's may need higher/parenteral dosing.
nutrients.source: Bischoff SC et al., ESPEN guideline on Clinical Nutrition in inflammatory bowel disease, Clin Nutr 2023

nutrients.mechanism: Chronic GI blood loss and malabsorption make iron-deficiency anaemia very common in IBD; correcting it improves fatigue and quality of life.
nutrients.dosage: Oral or IV iron per ECCO guidance depending on severity and disease activity (IV often preferred in active disease -- oral iron can worsen inflammation/symptoms)
nutrients.foodSources: Flour, potato (86.3mg, 663.8% RDA); Fenugreek Seeds / Methi (dried) (33.5mg, 257.7% RDA); Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (28.2mg, 216.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Oral iron may aggravate GI symptoms during active flares; IV iron is often preferred then.
nutrients.source: Dignass AU et al., European consensus on the diagnosis and management of iron deficiency and anaemia in IBD, J Crohns Colitis 2015

nutrients.mechanism: B12 is absorbed in the terminal ileum, a site frequently affected or resected in Crohn's disease -- deficiency is common and correctable.
nutrients.dosage: Screen and replace per deficiency (IM injections if ileal disease/resection, since oral absorption is impaired)
nutrients.foodSources: Clams (cooked) (98.9mcg, 4120.8% RDA); Beef Liver (cooked) (83.1mcg, 3462.5% RDA); Anchovies, canned in olive oil, with salt, drained (22.8mcg, 950.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Oral B12 is unreliable if terminal ileum is diseased or resected.
nutrients.source: Bischoff SC et al., ESPEN guideline on Clinical Nutrition in inflammatory bowel disease, Clin Nutr 2023

nutrients.mechanism: A high-fibre diet reduces the risk of diverticulitis recurrence once the acute episode has settled; during the acute phase a low-residue/clear-liquid diet is used instead.
nutrients.dosage: 25-30 g/day once acute inflammation has resolved, increased gradually
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do NOT increase fibre during an acute flare -- start low-residue, escalate only after symptoms settle, per clinician advice.
nutrients.source: Stollman N et al., American Gastroenterological Association Institute Guideline on the Management of Acute Diverticulitis, Gastroenterology 2015

nutrients.mechanism: Higher fibre intake is associated with lower colorectal cancer risk in large cohort studies -- this is a risk-reduction/primary-prevention association, not a treatment for existing cancer.
nutrients.dosage: 25-30 g/day as part of a varied, plant-forward diet (primary-prevention framing)
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Not a treatment for diagnosed cancer -- oncology-directed therapy is primary; discuss any dietary change with the treating oncology team, especially around surgery/chemotherapy.
nutrients.source: World Cancer Research Fund / AICR Continuous Update Project -- fibre, wholegrains and cancer

nutrients.mechanism: Adequate (not restricted) protein-calorie intake supports liver regeneration in acute hepatitis; protein restriction is only needed if hepatic encephalopathy develops, and is otherwise counter-productive.
nutrients.dosage: Maintain normal protein intake (~1.0-1.2 g/kg/day) unless encephalopathy is present, in which case a specialist should individualise
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do NOT routinely protein-restrict in uncomplicated acute hepatitis -- this was an outdated practice; only restrict under specialist guidance if encephalopathy develops. Avoid alcohol completely.
nutrients.source: Plauth M et al., ESPEN guideline on clinical nutrition in liver disease, Clin Nutr 2019

nutrients.mechanism: Dietary fibre increases stool bulk and softens stool, reducing transit time -- the best-evidenced first-line measure for functional constipation.
nutrients.dosage: 25-30 g/day (mixed soluble + insoluble), increased gradually with adequate fluids
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Increase fibre gradually to avoid bloating; ensure fluid intake rises alongside it.
nutrients.source: van der Schoot A et al., The Effect of Fiber Supplementation on Chronic Constipation in Adults: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of RCTs, Am J Clin Nutr 2022

nutrients.mechanism: Fibre supplementation softens stool and reduces straining, improving symptoms and bleeding in haemorrhoids -- one of the few interventions with pooled RCT evidence in this condition.
nutrients.dosage: 25-30 g/day, with 2 L/day fluid
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Introduce gradually; ensure adequate hydration alongside.
nutrients.source: Alonso-Coello P et al., Fiber for the treatment of hemorrhoids complications: a systematic review and meta-analysis, Am J Gastroenterol 2006

nutrients.mechanism: Villous atrophy from untreated coeliac disease impairs iron absorption; iron-deficiency anaemia is one of the most common presentations and usually corrects once a strict gluten-free diet is established.
nutrients.dosage: Replace per deficiency; re-check once mucosal healing is underway (usually improves without long-term supplementation once gluten-free)
nutrients.foodSources: Flour, potato (86.3mg, 663.8% RDA); Fenugreek Seeds / Methi (dried) (33.5mg, 257.7% RDA); Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (28.2mg, 216.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: A strict, lifelong gluten-free diet is the actual primary treatment -- iron repletion is secondary to that.
nutrients.source: Ludvigsson JF et al., Diagnosis and management of adult coeliac disease: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology, Gut 2014

nutrients.mechanism: Fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption from villous atrophy commonly causes vitamin D deficiency, contributing to reduced bone density seen at diagnosis.
nutrients.dosage: Correct confirmed deficiency; monitor bone density if longstanding untreated disease
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Improves with mucosal healing on a gluten-free diet, but initial repletion is often still needed.
nutrients.source: Ludvigsson JF et al., Diagnosis and management of adult coeliac disease: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology, Gut 2014

nutrients.mechanism: Combined with vitamin D malabsorption, calcium malabsorption contributes to the low bone mineral density common at coeliac diagnosis.
nutrients.dosage: 1,000-1,200 mg/day dietary calcium; supplement if dietary intake or absorption is inadequate
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Reassess once on a gluten-free diet -- absorption typically normalises with mucosal healing.
nutrients.source: Ludvigsson JF et al., Diagnosis and management of adult coeliac disease: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology, Gut 2014

nutrients.mechanism: Counter-intuitively, adequate (not restricted) dietary calcium binds oxalate in the gut and reduces oxalate absorption, lowering calcium-oxalate stone risk -- low-calcium diets increase stone risk.
nutrients.dosage: 1,000-1,200 mg/day from food (not supplements, which lack this protective gut effect and may raise risk)
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: The protective effect is specific to dietary calcium taken with meals -- calcium supplements without food do not show the same benefit and may increase risk.
nutrients.source: AUA Guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones (2014, updated 2026)

nutrients.mechanism: High sodium intake increases urinary calcium excretion, raising calcium-stone risk; restriction reduces recurrence.
nutrients.dosage: <2,300 mg/day
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Combine with adequate fluids and dietary (not supplemental) calcium for best effect.
nutrients.source: AUA Guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones

nutrients.mechanism: Plant sterol (beta-sitosterol) mixtures improve urinary symptom scores and flow rate in mild-to-moderate BPH in pooled RCT data, though long-term effect on disease progression is unproven.
nutrients.dosage: 60-130 mg/day beta-sitosterol (as used in the pooled trials)
nutrients.foodSources: Corn / Makai Oil (952mg, 119.0% RDA); Corn Oil (594mg, 74.2% RDA); Oil, corn (538mg, 67.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Long-term safety/efficacy beyond ~6 months is not well studied; does not replace medical/surgical therapy for significant obstruction.
nutrients.source: Wilt TJ et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 1999, CD001043

nutrients.mechanism: Omega-3 fatty acids have modest anti-inflammatory effects that may reduce OA pain, though effect sizes in trials are small.
nutrients.dosage: 1-3 g/day combined EPA/DHA
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High doses may increase bleeding risk with antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs.
nutrients.source: MacFarlane LA et al., Effects of Vitamin D and Marine Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation on Chronic Knee Pain in Older US Adults, Arthritis Rheumatol 2020

nutrients.mechanism: Observational studies link low vitamin D with OA severity, but RCTs of supplementation have not consistently shown symptomatic benefit except in deficient patients.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency; routine high-dose supplementation without testing is not evidence-supported for OA specifically
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap -- do not oversell benefit beyond correcting an actual deficiency.
nutrients.source: McAlindon TE et al., JAMA 2013 (vitamin D and knee OA RCT)

nutrients.mechanism: Marine omega-3 fatty acids reduce RA disease activity (tender/swollen joint counts, morning stiffness) and allow some patients to reduce NSAID use -- one of the better-evidenced dietary adjuncts in rheumatology.
nutrients.dosage: 2.7-3 g/day combined EPA/DHA for at least 3 months
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High doses can potentiate anticoagulants/antiplatelets, relevant in RA patients also on NSAIDs.
nutrients.source: Goldberg RJ, Katz J. Pain 2007 meta-analysis of n-3 fatty acids in inflammatory joint pain

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin D deficiency is common in RA and associated with higher inflammatory markers and disease activity; a dose-response meta-analysis of RCTs shows supplementation improves inflammatory and clinical outcome measures.
nutrients.dosage: Correct confirmed deficiency; typical trial doses ranged 400-100,000 IU depending on regimen -- follow a monitored replacement protocol rather than open-ended high-dose self-supplementation
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Supplementation corrects deficiency-related risk; it is not disease-modifying therapy on its own. Steroid use (common in RA) separately raises fracture risk, making replacement doubly relevant.
nutrients.evidenceTier: [Systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of RCTs]
nutrients.source: Al-Saoodi H et al., Effect of vitamin D on inflammatory and clinical outcomes in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, Nutrition Reviews 2024

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin C modestly lowers serum uric acid in RCTs, likely via increased renal urate excretion.
nutrients.dosage: 500 mg/day
nutrients.foodSources: Amla / Indian Gooseberry (raw) (600mg, 722.9% RDA); Guava / Amrood (raw) (228mg, 274.7% RDA); peppers, bell, red, raw, mini (220.5mg, 265.7% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Effect on uric acid is modest -- not a substitute for urate-lowering drugs (allopurinol/febuxostat) in patients who need them; high doses risk oxalate stones.
nutrients.source: Juraschek SP et al., meta-analysis, Arthritis Care Res 2011

nutrients.mechanism: Low-fat dairy intake (a major dietary calcium source) is associated with lower gout risk in large prospective cohorts, thought to be partly independent of its effect on uric acid.
nutrients.dosage: Low-fat dairy as part of a varied diet meeting the calcium RDA (~1,000 mg/day); pair with reducing high-fructose/sugar-sweetened drinks, beer, and purine-rich foods (organ meats, shellfish), which are the stronger, better-evidenced levers for flare frequency
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Gout is primarily managed by avoidance (purines, fructose, alcohol) and urate-lowering drugs -- this dairy/calcium association is a modest positive addition, not the primary intervention.
nutrients.source: Choi HK et al., Purine-rich foods, dairy and protein intake, and the risk of gout in men, N Engl J Med 2004

nutrients.mechanism: PMR is treated with long-term corticosteroids, which cause bone loss; calcium (with vitamin D) is standard co-prescribed bone protection.
nutrients.dosage: 1,000-1,200 mg/day dietary + supplement if intake is insufficient, alongside vitamin D and often a bisphosphonate
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Calcium/vitamin D alone is not sufficient bone protection on higher-dose/longer steroid courses -- follow local osteoporosis-prevention protocol.
nutrients.source: ACR Guideline for the Prevention and Treatment of Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis

nutrients.mechanism: Co-administered with calcium as standard steroid-induced osteoporosis prevention in PMR, which requires prolonged steroid courses.
nutrients.dosage: 800-1,000 IU/day (or per bone-health protocol)
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Part of a bone-protection package, not a treatment for PMR disease activity itself.
nutrients.source: ACR Guideline for the Prevention and Treatment of Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis

nutrients.mechanism: A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs shows vitamin D supplementation modestly improves eczema severity scores, mostly demonstrated in patients who were vitamin D-deficient at baseline.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency (typically 1,000-1,600 IU/day in trials)
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap for non-deficient patients -- test before treating where practical.
nutrients.source: Nielsen AY et al., Vitamin D Supplementation for Treating Atopic Dermatitis in Children and Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis, Nutrients 2024

nutrients.mechanism: Topical vitamin D analogues are a well-established first-line psoriasis treatment; oral/dietary vitamin D correction has a smaller but real effect, particularly relevant since psoriasis patients often run deficient.
nutrients.dosage: Correct confirmed deficiency (typically 800-2,000 IU/day); topical vitamin D analogues (prescribed) are the stronger-evidence route
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Oral supplementation alone is a modest adjunct -- not a substitute for topical/systemic psoriasis therapy.
nutrients.evidenceTier: [Guideline for topical use; observational for oral]
nutrients.source: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summary: Psoriasis

nutrients.mechanism: Omega-3 fatty acids have modest anti-inflammatory effects reported in some psoriasis trials, though results are inconsistent across studies.
nutrients.dosage: 3-4 g/day combined EPA/DHA if trialled
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence is mixed -- treat as adjunct only, alongside standard dermatology-directed therapy.
nutrients.source: Millsop JW et al., review of diet and psoriasis, J Am Acad Dermatol 2014

nutrients.mechanism: EPA-predominant omega-3 supplementation shows a modest antidepressant effect as an adjunct to standard treatment in meta-analyses, more consistently than DHA-predominant formulations.
nutrients.dosage: 1-2 g/day EPA-predominant fish oil, alongside (not instead of) standard depression treatment
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Not a substitute for psychotherapy/antidepressants in moderate-severe depression; discuss with the treating clinician.
nutrients.source: Liao Y et al., meta-analysis, Translational Psychiatry 2019

nutrients.mechanism: Low vitamin D is associated with depression in observational studies, but large RCTs of supplementation for depression treatment have been largely negative except in deficient subgroups.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency; not evidence-supported as a stand-alone antidepressant strategy
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap -- avoid overselling; large trials (VITAL-DEP) were negative for prevention of depression.
nutrients.source: Okereke OI et al., VITAL-DEP trial, JAMA 2020

nutrients.mechanism: Low folate/B12 status is associated with poorer antidepressant response in observational data; correcting a confirmed deficiency is reasonable, but folate augmentation in non-deficient patients has weak trial support.
nutrients.dosage: Correct confirmed deficiency per standard replacement dosing
nutrients.foodSources: Moong Dal / Green Gram (raw) (625mcg, 156.2% RDA); Chicken Liver (cooked) (578mcg, 144.5% RDA); FLOUR, CORN, YELLOW (FINE MEAL) (ENRICHED) (348mcg, 87.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap in non-deficient patients.
nutrients.source: Almeida OP et al., Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of folate and vitamin B12 for depression, International Psychogeriatrics 2015

nutrients.mechanism: In autoimmune (Hashimoto's) hypothyroidism, selenium supplementation reduces thyroid peroxidase antibody titres in several RCTs, though effect on clinical thyroid function/symptoms is less consistent.
nutrients.dosage: 200 mcg/day, typically trialled for 3-6 months
nutrients.foodSources: Brazil Nuts (1-2 nuts/day max) (1917mcg, 3485.5% RDA); brazil nuts, raw (377mcg, 685.5% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (328mcg, 596.4% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do not exceed the tolerable upper intake level (400 mcg/day) -- excess selenium is toxic and can itself impair thyroid function.
nutrients.source: Wichman J et al., meta-analysis of selenium in autoimmune thyroiditis, Thyroid 2016

nutrients.mechanism: Iron is a required cofactor for thyroid peroxidase; iron deficiency can blunt the response to levothyroxine and worsen hypothyroid symptoms.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed iron deficiency; separate iron and levothyroxine dosing by at least 4 hours (iron impairs levothyroxine absorption)
nutrients.foodSources: Flour, potato (86.3mg, 663.8% RDA); Fenugreek Seeds / Methi (dried) (33.5mg, 257.7% RDA); Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (28.2mg, 216.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Take levothyroxine and iron supplements several hours apart to avoid a drug-nutrient interaction that blunts thyroid hormone absorption.
nutrients.source: NIH ODS Iron Fact Sheet -- drug interactions with levothyroxine

nutrients.mechanism: Untreated/prolonged hyperthyroidism accelerates bone turnover and increases fracture risk; adequate calcium and vitamin D support bone protection alongside definitive thyroid treatment.
nutrients.dosage: 1,000-1,200 mg/day dietary calcium, with vitamin D sufficiency
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Does not treat the underlying hyperthyroidism -- antithyroid drugs/radioiodine/surgery remain primary therapy.
nutrients.source: ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism

nutrients.mechanism: High dietary fibre, particularly soluble fibre, slows glucose absorption and improves HbA1c and post-prandial glucose control -- one of the best-evidenced dietary interventions in T2DM.
nutrients.dosage: 25-38 g/day total fibre (ADA/dietary guideline target), including 5-10 g soluble fibre per main meal
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Increase gradually with fluids; may need to separate high-fibre meals from certain medications (levothyroxine, metformin) by 1-2 hours.
nutrients.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes -- Nutrition Therapy

nutrients.mechanism: Magnesium deficiency is common in T2DM and is linked to worse insulin sensitivity; supplementation in deficient/low-intake individuals modestly improves fasting glucose and HbA1c in meta-analyses.
nutrients.dosage: Aim to meet the RDA (~310-420 mg/day) through diet; supplement only if a deficiency is confirmed or intake is very low
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (627mg, 171.8% RDA); Pumpkin Seeds / Kaddu Beej (dried) (592mg, 162.2% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (511mg, 140.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High-dose supplements can cause diarrhoea; caution in renal impairment.
nutrients.source: Veronese N et al., meta-analysis of magnesium supplementation in T2DM, Eur J Clin Nutr 2016

nutrients.mechanism: Zinc is a cofactor for insulin storage/secretion; zinc status is often low in T2DM, and meta-analyses show modest improvements in fasting glucose and HbA1c with supplementation.
nutrients.dosage: Meet the RDA (~10 mg/day) through diet; formal supplementation trials have generally used ~30 mg/day zinc sulfate for defined courses
nutrients.foodSources: Oysters (cooked) (78.6mg, 786.0% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (10mg, 100.0% RDA); Hemp Seeds / Bhang (hulled) (9.9mg, 99.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Effect size is modest -- an adjunct to standard glycaemic therapy, not a replacement; high intakes can impair copper absorption.
nutrients.source: Wang X et al., Zinc supplementation improves glycemic control for diabetes prevention and management: a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, Am J Clin Nutr 2019

nutrients.mechanism: Iron-deficiency anaemia is, by definition, corrected by restoring iron stores -- dietary and/or supplemental iron is the primary, curative intervention (alongside treating the underlying cause of the deficiency).
nutrients.dosage: Oral ferrous sulfate/fumarate 100-200 mg elemental iron/day (or per local protocol); dietary iron from both haem (meat/poultry/fish) and non-haem (legumes, dark leafy greens, fortified grains) sources
nutrients.foodSources: Flour, potato (86.3mg, 663.8% RDA); Fenugreek Seeds / Methi (dried) (33.5mg, 257.7% RDA); Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (28.2mg, 216.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Common GI side effects (constipation, nausea); take with vitamin C-rich food, away from tea/coffee/calcium which inhibit absorption. Investigate and treat the underlying cause of deficiency (e.g. GI blood loss) -- don't just replace iron blindly.
nutrients.source: NIH ODS Iron Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin C converts dietary non-haem iron to a more absorbable form, meaningfully increasing iron uptake when taken together at the same meal.
nutrients.dosage: Pair iron-rich meals/supplements with a vitamin C source (citrus, amla, guava, bell pepper)
nutrients.foodSources: Amla / Indian Gooseberry (raw) (600mg, 722.9% RDA); Guava / Amrood (raw) (228mg, 274.7% RDA); peppers, bell, red, raw, mini (220.5mg, 265.7% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Absorption-enhancer only -- does not replace iron repletion itself.
nutrients.source: NIH ODS Iron Fact Sheet -- absorption enhancers/inhibitors

nutrients.mechanism: This is a nutrient-deficiency disease by definition -- restoring vitamin D status is the direct, curative treatment, supporting calcium absorption, bone mineralisation and muscle function.
nutrients.dosage: Loading regimen then maintenance per severity (e.g. 50,000 IU/week x 6-8 weeks for confirmed deficiency, then 800-2,000 IU/day maintenance) -- follow local/national protocol and re-check levels
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Excess vitamin D can cause hypercalcaemia -- follow a monitored replacement protocol rather than open-ended high-dose self-supplementation.
nutrients.source: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Evaluation, Treatment and Prevention of Vitamin D Deficiency

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin D deficiency is common in CFS/ME patients (often from reduced activity/sun exposure) and correcting a confirmed deficiency is reasonable general care, but there is no good evidence vitamin D treats CFS/ME itself.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency per standard protocol
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap -- no proven disease-modifying effect on CFS/ME symptoms specifically; treat as general health maintenance, not a CFS therapy.
nutrients.source: NICE Guideline: Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome

nutrients.mechanism: Cholera causes massive secretory diarrhoea; WHO oral rehydration solution (sodium, potassium, glucose) is lifesaving and the cornerstone of management alongside antibiotics in severe cases.
nutrients.dosage: WHO ORS, volume matched to ongoing stool losses; IV fluids if severely dehydrated/shocked
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Severe dehydration needs IV fluids first -- ORS alone is inadequate in shock; this is a medical emergency.
nutrients.source: WHO Cholera Fact Sheet & treatment guidance

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin C is a required cofactor for collagen synthesis, the main structural protein rebuilt during ligament healing; the biochemistry is well established, but direct outcome trials in simple ankle sprains specifically are sparse -- this is extrapolated from general connective-tissue-healing physiology, not sprain-specific RCTs.
nutrients.dosage: Ensure intake meets the RDA (~75-90 mg/day) through diet during the healing phase; no evidence that doses above this speed healing further
nutrients.foodSources: Amla / Indian Gooseberry (raw) (600mg, 722.9% RDA); Guava / Amrood (raw) (228mg, 274.7% RDA); peppers, bell, red, raw, mini (220.5mg, 265.7% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap -- extrapolated from general wound/connective-tissue-healing physiology rather than sprain-specific trials.
nutrients.source: NIH ODS Vitamin C Fact Sheet for Health Professionals -- collagen synthesis role

nutrients.mechanism: Adequate calcium and vitamin D support bone mineralisation during fracture healing and reduce future fracture risk, particularly relevant in fragility fractures.
nutrients.dosage: 1,000-1,200 mg/day dietary calcium
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Supports healing but does not replace surgical/orthopaedic fracture management.
nutrients.source: NOGG/National Osteoporosis Guideline Group -- bone health and fracture prevention

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin D is required for calcium absorption and bone mineralisation; combined calcium+vitamin D supplementation reduces fracture risk in at-risk (typically older, deficient) populations.
nutrients.dosage: 800-1,000 IU/day, paired with adequate calcium intake
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Benefit for fracture prevention is clearest in deficient/at-risk (e.g. care-home) populations, less so in replete community-dwelling adults.
nutrients.source: Bischoff-Ferrari HA et al., meta-analysis of vitamin D + calcium for fracture prevention, NEJM 2012

nutrients.mechanism: A randomised controlled trial of protein supplementation in elderly hip-fracture patients supports adequate protein intake for bone matrix formation and muscle strength during fracture healing and rehabilitation.
nutrients.dosage: 1.0-1.2 g/kg body weight/day during the healing/rehabilitation phase
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Individualise in significant renal impairment.
nutrients.source: Kalantar SH et al., Protein Supplementation for Hip Fracture Recovery in Elderly Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial, J Orthop Trauma 2026

nutrients.mechanism: Dietary protein competes with levodopa for absorption at the gut and blood-brain barrier; timing protein intake away from levodopa doses (rather than restricting total protein) improves drug efficacy and reduces 'on-off' fluctuations.
nutrients.dosage: Redistribute most protein to the evening meal, keeping daytime meals lower in protein around levodopa doses -- discuss timing with the treating neurologist, not a protein-restriction diet
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: This is a timing strategy, not protein restriction -- inadequate total protein risks sarcopenia, which is already a PD risk.
nutrients.source: Boelens Keun JT et al., Dietary Approaches to Improve Efficacy and Control Side Effects of Levodopa Therapy in Parkinson's Disease: A Systematic Review, Adv Nutr 2021

nutrients.mechanism: Constipation from autonomic dysfunction is near-universal in PD; dietary fibre and fluids are first-line non-drug management.
nutrients.dosage: 25-30 g/day with adequate fluids
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Introduce gradually.
nutrients.source: Beke MP, Managing Constipation and Its Risks in Parkinson's Disease: Is There a Role for Dietary Fiber?, Canadian Journal of Dietetic Practice and Research 2026

nutrients.mechanism: Older adults need more protein than the general RDA to counter anabolic resistance and preserve muscle mass; the PROT-AGE expert consensus is the reference standard for this.
nutrients.dosage: 1.0-1.2 g/kg body weight/day in healthy older adults, 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day if malnourished or acutely/chronically ill, distributed across meals (~25-30 g per meal)
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Higher intakes need individualising in significant chronic kidney disease -- discuss with a clinician/dietitian.
nutrients.source: Bauer J et al., PROT-AGE Study Group, J Am Med Dir Assoc 2013

nutrients.mechanism: Leucine is the amino acid that most directly triggers the muscle-protein-synthesis pathway (mTOR); leucine-rich protein sources or leucine-enriched supplements are used to boost the anabolic response per meal in sarcopenia.
nutrients.dosage: Aim for 2.5-3 g leucine per meal (met by ~25-30 g high-quality protein, e.g. dairy, soy, eggs, poultry)
nutrients.foodSources: FLOUR, SOY (DEFATTED) (4.4g, 159.7% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (4.1g, 150.5% RDA); mushrooms, maitake (3.8g, 139.3% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Best obtained through leucine-rich whole protein foods; isolated leucine supplementation has less robust long-term evidence than total protein adequacy.
nutrients.source: Devries MC et al., Leucine, Not Total Protein, Content of a Supplement Is the Primary Determinant of Muscle Protein Anabolic Responses in Healthy Older Women, J Nutr 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Vitamin D receptors are present in skeletal muscle; correcting deficiency improves muscle strength and reduces fall risk in deficient older adults, complementing protein/resistance-exercise strategies.
nutrients.dosage: Correct a confirmed deficiency (typically 800-1,000 IU/day maintenance)
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Benefit is clearest in those who are actually deficient -- not established as beneficial in vitamin D-replete individuals.
nutrients.source: Beaudart C et al., meta-analysis of vitamin D and muscle strength, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014

nutrients.mechanism: Observational studies associate higher omega-3/fish intake with lower dementia risk, but RCTs of omega-3 supplementation once dementia is established have been largely disappointing.
nutrients.dosage: Dietary oily fish intake as part of a Mediterranean/MIND dietary pattern is the better-evidenced framing; supplement trials for established Alzheimer's have not shown consistent cognitive benefit
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap for treating established disease -- framed here as a dietary-pattern, risk-reduction association rather than a treatment.
nutrients.evidenceTier: [Cochrane systematic review, negative for treatment -- stated honestly]
nutrients.source: Burckhardt M et al., Omega-3 fatty acids for the treatment of dementia, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2016, CD009002

nutrients.mechanism: B12/folate deficiency causes a reversible cognitive impairment that can mimic or worsen dementia; screening for and correcting deficiency is standard of care in any new cognitive decline work-up, though correction does not reverse established Alzheimer's pathology.
nutrients.dosage: Screen and replace per confirmed deficiency
nutrients.foodSources: Clams (cooked) (98.9mcg, 4120.8% RDA); Beef Liver (cooked) (83.1mcg, 3462.5% RDA); Anchovies, canned in olive oil, with salt, drained (22.8mcg, 950.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Large homocysteine-lowering B-vitamin trials (e.g. VITACOG) did not show a clear reduction in Alzheimer's progression despite lowering homocysteine -- correction is about excluding a reversible contributor, not treating Alzheimer's itself.
nutrients.source: NICE Guideline: Dementia -- assessment, management and support

nutrients.mechanism: Vascular dementia progression tracks with cerebrovascular risk factor control; the same sodium-restricted, potassium-rich dietary pattern used for stroke/hypertension prevention is the relevant evidence base here (secondary prevention, not a direct cognitive treatment).
nutrients.dosage: <2,300 mg/day sodium as part of a DASH/Mediterranean-pattern diet
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: This is a vascular-risk-reduction strategy, not a direct treatment for existing cognitive impairment.
nutrients.source: AHA/ASA 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack

nutrients.mechanism: In patients with alcohol use disorder or malnutrition, delirium can be caused or worsened by Wernicke's encephalopathy (thiamine deficiency) -- empirical thiamine before glucose is a well-known emergency-medicine safety step in this specific subgroup.
nutrients.dosage: IV/IM thiamine (per local emergency protocol) before/with any glucose administration in at-risk patients (alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, bariatric surgery history)
nutrients.foodSources: Nutritional Yeast (14.3mg, 1243.5% RDA); Flour, all-purpose, enriched (1.9mg, 167.0% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (1.6mg, 142.6% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Relevant only to the alcohol-use-disorder/malnutrition subgroup of delirium, not delirium in general, which has many other causes needing their own work-up.
nutrients.source: Royal College of Physicians / NICE guidance on Wernicke's encephalopathy prevention

nutrients.mechanism: As with Alzheimer's, a Mediterranean/MIND dietary pattern rich in omega-3s is associated with slower cognitive decline in observational cohorts, though RCT evidence specifically for reversing MCI is limited.
nutrients.dosage: Dietary pattern emphasis (oily fish, nuts, olive oil) rather than isolated high-dose supplementation
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Evidence gap for isolated supplementation reversing/halting MCI progression -- framed as a dietary-pattern association.
nutrients.source: Morris MC et al., MIND diet and cognitive decline, Alzheimers Dement 2015

nutrients.mechanism: A low-glycemic-load diet (less refined sugar, white bread and white rice; more whole grains and legumes) has repeatedly, independently reduced inflammatory acne lesion counts in randomised controlled trials, likely via lower insulin/IGF-1 signalling to the sebaceous gland.
nutrients.dosage: Swap high-glycemic-index carbohydrates for low-glycemic-index/whole-grain alternatives day to day, rather than a fixed gram target
nutrients.foodSources: Sugars, granulated (99.6g, 76.6% RDA); Flour, cassava (87.3g, 67.2% RDA); Fonio, grain, dry, raw (81.3g, 62.5% RDA)
nutrients.caution: An adjunct alongside standard topical/oral acne treatment, not a substitute for it.
nutrients.source: Smith RN et al., A low-glycemic-load diet improves symptoms in acne vulgaris patients: a randomized controlled trial, Am J Clin Nutr 2007

nutrients.mechanism: Acne patients often show lower serum zinc, and zinc supplementation as an adjunct has shown a significant reduction in inflammatory lesion counts in a systematic review and meta-analysis.
nutrients.dosage: Discuss dose with a doctor or pharmacist -- typical trial doses are in the 30-45 mg elemental zinc/day range, best taken with food to reduce nausea
nutrients.foodSources: Oysters (cooked) (78.6mg, 786.0% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (10mg, 100.0% RDA); Hemp Seeds / Bhang (hulled) (9.9mg, 99.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Underlying trials are small and heterogeneous; long-term high-dose zinc can cause copper deficiency, so this is an adjunct, not a first-line treatment.
nutrients.source: Yee BE et al., Serum zinc levels and efficacy of zinc treatment in acne vulgaris: A systematic review and meta-analysis, Dermatol Ther 2020

nutrients.mechanism: Dietary sodium restriction, as part of the DASH dietary pattern, meaningfully lowers blood pressure; a meta-analysis of 30 RCTs found the DASH diet reduced systolic BP by 3-7 mmHg and diastolic BP by 2.5-3.5 mmHg.
nutrients.dosage: <2,300 mg/day sodium as part of a DASH-pattern diet (fruit, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy)
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Indian diets (pickles, papad, added salt) are typically very high in sodium -- this is often the single highest-yield dietary change available.
nutrients.source: Saneei P et al., DASH diet and blood pressure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, Nutr Metab Cardiovasc Dis 2014

nutrients.mechanism: Higher dietary potassium intake (fruit, vegetables, legumes) is independently associated with lower blood pressure and is a core component of the DASH pattern.
nutrients.dosage: Meet the RDA (~3,000-3,400 mg/day) through diet -- fruit, vegetables, legumes, dairy
nutrients.foodSources: FLOUR, SOY (DEFATTED) (2520mg, 84.0% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (2480mg, 82.7% RDA); coconut flour (2300mg, 76.7% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Avoid potassium supplements without medical advice in kidney disease or if on ACE-inhibitors/ARBs/potassium-sparing diuretics -- risk of hyperkalaemia.
nutrients.evidenceTier: [Systematic review of RCTs, part of the DASH evidence base]
nutrients.source: Saneei P et al., DASH diet and blood pressure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, Nutr Metab Cardiovasc Dis 2014

nutrients.mechanism: Matching insulin dose to carbohydrate intake (carbohydrate counting) is the central dietary skill in type 1 diabetes management -- it is not about restricting carbohydrate, but about accurate, consistent dosing around it.
nutrients.dosage: Individualised insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio, taught through structured diabetes education -- not a fixed gram target
nutrients.foodSources: Sugars, granulated (99.6g, 76.6% RDA); Flour, cassava (87.3g, 67.2% RDA); Fonio, grain, dry, raw (81.3g, 62.5% RDA)
nutrients.caution: This is a dosing-matching skill, not a restrictive diet -- under-eating to avoid injecting insulin is dangerous and should never be encouraged.
nutrients.source: ISPAD Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines 2022: Diabetes in adolescence

nutrients.mechanism: High-fibre foods increase satiety and reduce overall energy intake, supporting sustainable weight loss as part of a calorie-reduced diet.
nutrients.dosage: 25-38 g/day total fibre, from whole grains, legumes, vegetables and fruit
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Increase gradually with adequate fluids to avoid bloating.
nutrients.source: NICE Obesity: identification, assessment and management guideline

nutrients.mechanism: Higher dietary protein within a calorie-reduced diet increases satiety and helps preserve lean muscle mass during weight loss, compared with lower-protein calorie-matched diets.
nutrients.dosage: 1.2-1.6 g/kg body weight/day within an overall calorie-reduced diet
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Individualise in significant renal impairment.
nutrients.source: NICE Obesity: identification, assessment and management guideline

nutrients.mechanism: Soluble fibre (psyllium, oats, legumes) binds bile acids and reduces cholesterol reabsorption, lowering LDL cholesterol; a meta-analysis found it meaningfully enhances the LDL-lowering effect of statins as an adjunct.
nutrients.dosage: 10-25 g/day soluble fibre
nutrients.foodSources: Psyllium Husk / Isabgol (dried) (71g, 710.0% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (ground) (11g, 110.0% RDA); Chia Seeds (dried) (10g, 100.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Introduce gradually with fluids to avoid bloating; take at a different time from other medications if advised, since fibre can affect absorption.
nutrients.source: Brum J et al., Meta-Analysis of Usefulness of Psyllium Fiber as Adjuvant Antilipid Therapy, Am J Cardiol 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Plant sterols/stanols competitively inhibit cholesterol absorption in the gut; a large meta-analysis found LDL cholesterol reductions of 6-12% on average at typical intakes.
nutrients.dosage: ~2 g/day plant sterols/stanols (fortified spreads, yoghurt drinks) or from natural sources (vegetable oils, nuts, seeds)
nutrients.foodSources: Corn / Makai Oil (952mg, 119.0% RDA); Corn Oil (594mg, 74.2% RDA); Oil, corn (538mg, 67.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Effect plateaus above ~3g/day; not a substitute for statin therapy where indicated -- an adjunct alongside it.
nutrients.source: Abumweis SS et al., Plant sterols/stanols as cholesterol lowering agents: a meta-analysis of RCTs, Food Nutr Res 2008

nutrients.mechanism: Marine omega-3 fatty acids lower triglycerides, the lipid parameter they affect most consistently; effect on LDL cholesterol specifically is more modest.
nutrients.dosage: 2-4 g/day combined EPA/DHA for triglyceride-lowering (higher than the general cardiovascular-health dose)
nutrients.foodSources: ground flaxseed meal (23.5g, 1467.5% RDA); Flaxseeds / Alsi (raw) (22.8g, 1425.0% RDA); Flaxseed, ground (19.4g, 1213.8% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High doses can potentiate antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs; discuss with a doctor if triglycerides are very high, since prescription-strength omega-3 may be appropriate instead of supplements.
nutrients.source: Skulas-Ray AC et al., Omega-3 Fatty Acids for the Management of Hypertriglyceridemia: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, Circulation 2019

nutrients.mechanism: High dietary fibre improves several metabolic syndrome components simultaneously -- glycaemic control, lipid profile and satiety-driven weight management -- consistent with its established role in T2DM and dyslipidaemia individually.
nutrients.dosage: 25-38 g/day total fibre
nutrients.foodSources: Sorghum bran, white, unenriched, dry, raw (43.9g, 156.9% RDA); coconut flour (39.5g, 141.1% RDA); ground flaxseed meal (36.7g, 131.1% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Increase gradually with adequate fluids; address each component (BP, lipids, glucose) with its own specific management as well -- fibre alone will not resolve the syndrome.
nutrients.source: IDF Consensus Worldwide Definition of the Metabolic Syndrome

nutrients.mechanism: In CKD stages 3-5, higher protein intake increases the kidneys' filtration workload and is associated with faster progression; KDIGO's 2024 guideline recommends moderating (not eliminating) protein intake.
nutrients.dosage: ~0.8 g/kg body weight/day; avoid intakes above 1.3 g/kg/day if at risk of progression
nutrients.foodSources: Egg, white, dried (79.9g, 159.8% RDA); Flour, soy, defatted (51.1g, 102.2% RDA); Egg, whole, dried (48.1g, 96.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do not restrict below this without dietitian supervision -- under-nutrition is a real risk, especially in older adults; needs vary by CKD stage and dialysis status.
nutrients.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD

nutrients.mechanism: Sodium restriction reduces blood pressure and fluid overload in CKD, both of which independently drive faster progression and cardiovascular risk.
nutrients.dosage: <2,000 mg/day sodium (<5 g/day salt)
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Indian diets (pickles, papad, added salt, processed snacks) are typically high in sodium -- often the highest-yield single dietary change in CKD.
nutrients.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD

nutrients.mechanism: Moderate sodium restriction is a core part of managing ascites in cirrhosis, reducing fluid retention alongside prescribed diuretics.
nutrients.dosage: ~2,000 mg/day sodium (about 88 mmol/day) if ascites is present
nutrients.foodSources: Salt; iodized (40700mg, 1769.6% RDA); Table Salt / Namak (iodised) (38758mg, 1685.1% RDA); Rock Salt / Sendha Namak (38000mg, 1652.2% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do not restrict further without dietitian input -- over-restriction can worsen appetite and nutritional status, which is already a risk in cirrhosis.
nutrients.source: AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management of Ascites, Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis and Hepatorenal Syndrome

nutrients.mechanism: A 2024 Cochrane review found vitamin D supplementation gives little to no overall reduction in COPD exacerbation rate (high-certainty evidence) -- BUT a genuine subgroup benefit exists in patients with severe baseline vitamin D deficiency (25(OH)D below 25 nmol/L / 10 ng/mL), where supplementation did reduce moderate/severe exacerbations. This is a deficiency-correction effect, not a general COPD treatment.
nutrients.dosage: Check vitamin D level first; supplement only if genuinely deficient, per your doctor's dosing protocol -- routine supplementation in a non-deficient COPD patient has no shown benefit
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Do not self-supplement at high dose without a checked level -- benefit is confined to the deficient subgroup, and excess vitamin D can cause hypercalcaemia.
nutrients.source: Williamson A et al., Vitamin D for the management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2024

nutrients.mechanism: A meta-analysis of 29 RCTs (n=63,897) found calcium supplementation, alone or with vitamin D, reduced fracture risk by 12% overall -- rising to 24% with good compliance (>80%) at a dose of 1,200 mg/day or more. One of the largest, most robust evidence bases behind any nutrient recommendation in this database.
nutrients.dosage: 1,000-1,200 mg/day total (diet + supplement combined) -- higher intakes did not show added benefit in this meta-analysis
nutrients.foodSources: Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (2003mg, 200.3% RDA); American pasteurized process cheese food, sliced, individually wrapped (1680mg, 168.0% RDA); American pasteurized prepared cheese product, with added vitamin D, sliced, individually wrapped (1670mg, 167.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High-dose calcium supplementation (without dietary calcium accounted for) has been linked to kidney stones and, in some analyses, cardiovascular risk -- prioritise dietary sources and discuss supplement dosing with a doctor.
nutrients.source: Tang BM et al., Use of calcium or calcium in combination with vitamin D supplementation to prevent fractures and bone loss in people aged 50 years and older: a meta-analysis, Lancet 2007

nutrients.mechanism: In the same meta-analysis, vitamin D combined with calcium supported the same fracture-risk reduction, with the clearest benefit in those with marginal or low vitamin D status -- a population-level concern given widespread vitamin D deficiency in India.
nutrients.dosage: 800-1,000 IU/day maintenance for most adults; higher loading doses if a deficiency is confirmed on testing, per a monitored protocol
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Excess vitamin D can cause hypercalcaemia -- follow a monitored replacement protocol for confirmed deficiency rather than open-ended high-dose self-supplementation.
nutrients.source: Tang BM et al., Use of calcium or calcium in combination with vitamin D supplementation to prevent fractures and bone loss in people aged 50 years and older: a meta-analysis, Lancet 2007

nutrients.mechanism: Hookworm feeds on blood at its intestinal attachment site -- a heavy burden can cause loss of up to 250 mL of blood and 29 mg of iron per day, directly driving iron-deficiency anaemia. Deworming stops the ongoing loss but does not by itself replenish already-depleted iron stores, so iron replacement is standard adjunct care alongside anthelmintic treatment, not a substitute for it.
nutrients.dosage: Oral ferrous sulfate/fumarate per standard iron-deficiency-anaemia dosing once deworming has been given; dietary iron from haem and non-haem sources
nutrients.foodSources: Flour, potato (86.3mg, 663.8% RDA); Fenugreek Seeds / Methi (dried) (33.5mg, 257.7% RDA); Dried Drumstick Leaves / Moringa (powder) (28.2mg, 216.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Treat the worm infestation itself first/alongside -- iron alone does not stop ongoing blood loss if the infection is not also treated.
nutrients.source: Stoltzfus RJ et al., Hookworm control as a strategy to prevent iron deficiency, Nutrition Reviews 1997

nutrients.mechanism: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency causes fat malabsorption, and a meta-analysis found vitamin D deficiency in 57.6% of chronic pancreatitis patients -- the most prevalent fat-soluble vitamin deficiency in this condition, and clinically significant because it raises the risk of metabolic bone disease on top of the pancreatic disease itself.
nutrients.dosage: Check vitamin D level and correct a confirmed deficiency per standard protocol, alongside pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy which improves fat (and so fat-soluble vitamin) absorption
nutrients.foodSources: Cod Liver Oil (250mcg, 1428.6% RDA); Egg, yolk, dried (15.7mcg, 89.7% RDA); Swordfish (cooked) (14.5mcg, 82.9% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Correcting deficiency does not treat the pancreatitis itself -- enzyme replacement and the underlying disease still need their own management; excess vitamin D can cause hypercalcaemia, so follow a monitored protocol.
nutrients.source: Hoogenboom SA et al., Systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in patients with chronic pancreatitis, Pancreatology 2016

nutrients.mechanism: This is a nutrient-deficiency disease by definition -- restoring B12 status is the direct, curative treatment for the deficiency, and the only way to prevent or arrest irreversible neurological damage (subacute combined degeneration) from ongoing deficiency.
nutrients.dosage: IM B12 injections (loading then maintenance per local protocol), or high-dose oral (1,000-2,000mcg/day) once pernicious anaemia/malabsorption is excluded or being separately managed
nutrients.foodSources: Clams (cooked) (98.9mcg, 4120.8% RDA); Beef Liver (cooked) (83.1mcg, 3462.5% RDA); Anchovies, canned in olive oil, with salt, drained (22.8mcg, 950.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Neurological symptoms need prompt treatment -- do not wait for full diagnostic workup to start replacement if deficiency is strongly suspected and B12 has been sent. Lifelong replacement is usually needed for pernicious anaemia or malabsorption.
nutrients.source: Naik S et al., Identification of vitamin B12 deficiency in vegetarian Indians, British Journal of Nutrition 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Folate deficiency produces the same megaloblastic/macrocytic anaemia picture as B12 deficiency and is, by definition, corrected by restoring folate status -- but B12 must be checked and treated first/alongside, since giving folate alone can mask a B12 deficiency's blood picture while its neurological damage continues to progress.
nutrients.dosage: Oral folic acid per standard deficiency-replacement dosing, only after (or alongside) confirming B12 status
nutrients.foodSources: Moong Dal / Green Gram (raw) (625mcg, 156.2% RDA); Chicken Liver (cooked) (578mcg, 144.5% RDA); FLOUR, CORN, YELLOW (FINE MEAL) (ENRICHED) (348mcg, 87.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: Never treat with folate alone without checking B12 first -- this is a well-recognised way to miss and worsen B12-deficiency neuropathy.
nutrients.source: Naik S et al., Identification of vitamin B12 deficiency in vegetarian Indians, British Journal of Nutrition 2018

nutrients.mechanism: Zinc has a role in cell-mediated immunity against HPV-infected keratinocytes. Individual randomised placebo-controlled trials are genuinely mixed -- Al-Gurairi 2002 found high-dose oral zinc sulphate highly effective for recalcitrant warts, while a later double-blind RCT (Lopez-Garcia 2009, honestly titled 'too good to be true?') found no significant benefit over placebo -- but a 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis pooling the available RCTs found a significant overall reduction in recurrence and improved clearance.
nutrients.dosage: Typically dosed at 10mg/kg/day (up to 600mg/day) in the trials showing benefit, for treatment-resistant/recalcitrant warts specifically -- not first-line for simple warts, which usually resolve with topical treatment or watchful waiting alone
nutrients.foodSources: Oysters (cooked) (78.6mg, 786.0% RDA); pumpkin seeds (pepitas), raw (10mg, 100.0% RDA); Hemp Seeds / Bhang (hulled) (9.9mg, 99.0% RDA)
nutrients.caution: High-dose zinc can cause GI upset and, with prolonged use, copper deficiency -- reserve for recalcitrant cases and use a defined course rather than open-ended supplementation; evidence is real but genuinely mixed at the individual-trial level.
nutrients.source: Wang CC et al., Oral zinc sulphate reduces the recurrence rate and provides significant therapeutic effects for viral warts: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, PLoS One 2025
